pointers.sentence: A refusal uses an exception Django already has: `SuspiciousOperation`, a 400 when a view lets it escape (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`), `ValidationError`, `LookupError`, `ValueError`, or a false answer from a check.
`strip_tags` feeds the text to an HTML parser, `MLStripper`, and repeats while a pass still removes a tag (`django/utils/html.py:strip_tags`).

An end tag now pops the stack of open tags only when it closes the tag opened last; the comment there says this avoids a linear scan for each unmatched one (`django/utils/text.py:TruncateHTMLParser.handle_endtag`).
At this commit it hands each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper` (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`; [Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md)).
At this commit it hands each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper` (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`; [Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md)).

With its use_l10n argument true, the default, a value that can be made a decimal goes to `number_format`; otherwise the leading digits of its text are grouped by one substitution over them reversed, linear in their length (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:intcomma`; [Humanize: `naturaltime`, `intcomma` and the other filters](../contrib/humanize.md)).

It now returns its input as given when the decimal's digits and the absolute value of its exponent come to more than 200: `"1e200"` comes back as `"1e200"`, and `"1e199"` is written out in its 200 digits (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:floatformat`; [The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md)).
Several guards here stop a long URL before it is split, at one bound: `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, 2,048 characters (`django/utils/http.py`).

The URL linker, `django.utils.html.urlize` and the `urlize` and `urlizetrunc` filters (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer`), had fixes in 2024: for input with very many brackets (CVE-2024-38875, 5.0.7), very large input with a particular sequence of characters (CVE-2024-41990, 5.0.8; CVE-2024-45230, 5.0.9 and 5.1.1), and input with very many Unicode characters, which reached the admin's URL widget too (CVE-2024-41991, 5.0.8).

At this commit a word whose text, once its punctuation is trimmed, is longer than `MAX_URL_LENGTH` is not tried as a URL (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`), and trimming a word's punctuation is linear: each kind of bracket is counted once, in a `CountsDict`, the trimmed pieces are joined once, and only the text from the last "&" is unescaped to judge a trailing ";" (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.trim_punctuation`).

At this commit a word whose text, once its punctuation is trimmed, is longer than `MAX_URL_LENGTH` is not tried as a URL (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`), and trimming a word's punctuation is linear: each kind of bracket is counted once, in a `CountsDict`, the trimmed pieces are joined once, and only the text from the last "&" is unescaped to judge a trailing ";" (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.trim_punctuation`).

`AdminURLFieldWidget` links its value only when its validator, by default `URLValidator`, accepts it, and the validator refuses a URL over `URLValidator.max_length`, `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, before it splits it (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:AdminURLFieldWidget.get_context`).

Each judges the URL it is to redirect to with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, which refuses one over `MAX_URL_LENGTH` before splitting it (`django/utils/http.py:_url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`; [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md#urls-that-came-from-a-client)).

Each judges the URL it is to redirect to with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, which refuses one over `MAX_URL_LENGTH` before splitting it (`django/utils/http.py:_url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`; [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md#urls-that-came-from-a-client)).

The redirects followed (CVE-2025-64458, 5.1.14 and 5.2.8): `HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__`, and so `redirect`, raises `DisallowedRedirect` for a `"Location"` longer than `MAX_URL_REDIRECT_LENGTH`, 16,384 characters, before it splits the target (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__`; [The response object](../http/response.md#redirects)).
It now looks only at what precedes the first colon, and never calls `urllib.parse.urlsplit` (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.to_python`).

`is_valid_ipv6_address` now refuses text longer than `MAX_IPV6_ADDRESS_LENGTH`, 39 characters, eight groups of four and their colons, before `ipaddress` parses it, and `clean_ipv6_address` text longer than its max_length, by default the same (`django/utils/ipv6.py:_ipv6_address_from_str`).
`django.forms.GenericIPAddressField` takes 39 as its max_length unless given another, and passes it to `clean_ipv6_address` (`django/forms/fields.py:GenericIPAddressField`).

It now cuts a code longer than `LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH`, 500 characters, at its last hyphen within the limit, and refuses it with `LookupError` if it has none there or strict is true (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_supported_language_variant`).

At this commit it is not cached: it refuses a code over the limit, and asks the cached `translation_catalog_exists`, which holds 1,000 codes, about the rest (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:check_for_language`; [Choosing a language: `LocaleMiddleware`](../i18n/choosing.md#supported-codes)).

`ASGIRequest.__init__` now gathers each header's values in a list and joins them once, with commas, or for `"cookie"` with a semicolon and a space (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope)).

`body` refuses a declared length over the limit before reading, and then, when the stream can seek, as an ASGI request's can, measures it and raises `RequestDataTooBig` if it is over (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.body`; [The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](../http/body.md#under-asgi)).

`MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input` decides whether files stay in memory by the size of a stream that can seek; a WSGI request's `LimitedStream` cannot, and there the header, which it enforces, still decides (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`; [Multipart parsing and upload handlers](../http/uploads.md#memory-or-disk)).

At this commit the parser strips a chunk's white space, reads further chunks whole until the stripped length is a multiple of four, and joins the pieces once before decoding (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

Since 6.1 it reads only a node's own text, and `check_element_type` raises `SuspiciousOperation` for a child element with content of its own, so a nested element with content is refused, not walked (`django/core/serializers/xml_serializer.py:check_element_type`; [What changed in caching, files, signals, serialization and pagination](caching-files-signals.md)).

Past the limit, by default `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS`, 198, the reader raises `ValueError` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKBReader`; [Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](../contrib/geometries.md#geosgeometry)).

Past the limit, by default `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS`, 198, the reader raises `ValueError` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKBReader`; [Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](../contrib/geometries.md#geosgeometry)).

GeoJSON is parsed by GDAL, and GDAL's WKB of it is counted at the default limit, whatever max_geom_collections says (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/geometries.py:OGRGeometry._geos_ptr`); geometries read back from the database are read with no limit ([Spatial fields: the geometry fields and `RasterField`](../contrib/spatial-fields.md)).

The form field takes it too, and there `None` keeps the default, so a model field given `None` still makes a form field that refuses past 198 (`django/contrib/gis/forms/fields.py:GeometryField.__init__`).
